name: Digital Nomad Visa (Visado para Teletrabajadores de Carácter Internacional)

requirement_groups.name: Residence authorization (applied from within Spain — leads to PR)

value.note: 200% of SMI stated on a 14-payment annual basis, divided into 12 monthly instalments: (1221 * 14 * 2) / 12 = 2849. The ratio here (2.333...) is the EFFECTIVE monthly multiplier relative to the 14-payment monthly SMI figure, not a literal '200%' — flagged explicitly so the formula's arithmetic is transparent rather than mysterious.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires remote income from foreign employers/clients of at least approximately €2,849/month (200% of the 2026 minimum wage).
requirements.fix_path: Increase remote income to the required level.

value.note: no more than 20% of total income may be Spanish-sourced

requirements.blocker_text: This requires that no more than 20% of total income come from Spanish sources — the bulk must be genuinely foreign.
This requires a university degree from a recognised institution, or at least 3 years of relevant professional experience.
This requires the foreign employer or clients to have been operating for at least 1 year.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract or client contracts with income traceable via bank certificates matching the contract terms
Degree certificate or documented 3+ years' professional experience
Payslips or invoices covering the last 3 months

outcome.duration_length: consular visa route: 1 year; UGE-CE residence-authorization route (from within Spain): up to 3 years, renewable in 2-year periods

sources.title: BOE — Ley 28/2022 (Startup Law) amending Ley 14/2013, Digital Nomad Visa provisions

notes: FORMULA VALUE, tier-1 confirmed: exactly 200% of SMI, computed from the 14-payment annual figure divided into 12 monthly instalments — (€1,221 × 14 × 2) / 12 ≈ €2,849/month. HIGH STALE-DATA RISK: multiple tier-3 sites still publish €2,700, €2,646, or €2,368/month, all based on the 2024 or 2025 SMI before the February 2026 increase — this is the single most common stale figure found across all Spain sources during research. Optional Beckham-style tax regime available: flat 24% IRPF on Spanish-source employment income up to €600,000/year (vs. progressive rates up to ~47-50%) — a genuinely distinctive fiscal incentive not present on any digital-nomad-equivalent route in UK/Germany/Netherlands/Portugal, worth surfacing prominently since it materially changes the route's real-world attractiveness beyond the immigration terms alone; not modeled as a formal schema field, captured in notes only pending a decision on whether tax treatment deserves its own schema element across the whole dataset. Processing is genuinely fast for the UGE-CE route: approximately 20 business days, with approval by positive administrative silence if no response — a real operational advantage over most other routes in this dataset, most of which face backlog-driven delays (see Portugal's AIMA situation for the opposite extreme).
